solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man getting sack, as if Mrs Thatcher could be bothered

indicators.note: something bothered is ruffled and disturbed, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A politician is sacked, and Margaret Thatcher is wondered about as if she might care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting sack' suggests being fired, which fits the Thatcher surface; FATHER CHRISTMAS is the man who gets a sack of presents to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa is pictured hauling a big bag of toys, so he is the man with a sack.

clue.text: Follower of fashion with directions for making punch?

indicators.note: read as holding within, so one word carries the other inside it

parts.note: a fist is what you punch with
the word a recipe repeats in its directions

explanation.surface: A trendy party-goer follows the recipe for a bowl of punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the clue is a recipe's instruction put inside a fist; 'punch' looks like the drink but is the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist eagerly takes up each passing craze, so is a follower of fashion.

clue.text: Take in run, coming in second

indicators.note: something coming in enters, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A runner receives a message while finishing second.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is to deceive them, which is what a trick does as a verb.

clue.text: One's going to sea, so it's said — more easily with this?

definitions.note: read with 'sea' heard as 'see': one sees more easily with this

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the sound of the words counts

parts.note: one is going to (I'll) the sea (ocean)

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a voyage, wondering if it will go more easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash pivots: 'sea' also serves as 'see', so the end says you see more easily with this.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye lotion soothes and clears the eyes, helping vision, so one sees more easily with it.

clue.text: Doctor Who won't fight no dalek, ultimately!

parts.note: a conscientious objector refuses to fight

indicators.note: ultimately points at the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

explanation.surface: A rallying cry that the Time Lord should not battle a Dalek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' runs together as the TV show, but 'Doctor' is the definition and 'Who' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to falsify them, just as one cooks the books.

clue.text: Again correct to swallow tablets to get most high

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece is held within the other

explanation.surface: An editor revising copy pops pills to get as high as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' suggests drugs, which the tablets support, but here it means high-pitched.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice is thin and high-pitched, so the reediest is the most shrill in tone.

clue.text: Writing on reflection remains a great success

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: Thinking back, the surviving manuscripts turned out to be a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash, or smash hit, is a show or record that wins huge popularity.

clue.text: Entering harbour, just losing way, a trip provider

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these letters sit within the other word
losing something means it is dropped, so letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A boat slips into port at the last minute, ferrying holidaymakers.
explanation.walkthrough: JU and A go into MARINA. A 'trip' here is a drug-induced experience, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis induces a hallucinatory high, which slang calls a trip, so it provides one.

clue.text: Did pilot hit the roof crossing top of this?

indicators.note: crossing means going across and so straddling, holding the letter inside

parts.note: to see red is to get furious

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A pilot loses their temper, or perhaps strikes the hangar roof flying over it.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SEE RED after the S. 'Hit the roof' plays on aircraft, but means getting angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to guide a vessel's course, which is to steer it.

clue.text: Stress caused by commuter journey?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to emphasise a point forcefully
second meaning: motoring back from work

explanation.surface: Anxiety brought on by the daily trip to and from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' reads as strain from travel, but it is a verb: to make a point clear.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to emphasise it, and a commuter literally motors home.

clue.text: Ace to welcome having time off for match

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a letter drops out

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tennis star receives a rest day before the big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' and 'match' both suggest tennis, but match is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts agree when they correspond, the same as when they match.

clue.text: Writer's well popular, returning to peak!

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words after it are read from the end

parts.note: PK is the abbreviation for peak

explanation.surface: A popular writer climbs back to the summit of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's well' sounds like an author doing nicely, but a well is a reservoir for a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkpot is the small container a pen is dipped into, a reservoir of ink.

clue.text: Bird with judge in black coat, not far ahead

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge in a black robe sits near the front with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black coat' sounds like the judge's gown; it is the verb tar.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird with a churring call, also called a goatsucker.

clue.text: Urban dweller to have secure fences

indicators.note: a fence encloses ground, so one piece surrounds the other

explanation.surface: A city resident puts up secure fencing round their plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A townie is a colloquial word for someone from a town rather than the countryside.

clue.text: One having a race with a "condition" — not well at finish

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a term of a contract is a condition

explanation.surface: A runner with a medical condition enters a race but feels poorly at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A race here is a millrace, the channel of water that drives a mill wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermill is powered by a millrace, the fast stream channelled to turn its wheel.

clue.text: Barmaids worked on as engineer was called

definitions.note: the answer is the name the engineer was called

indicators.note: something worked on is reshaped, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Bar staff put in a shift, labouring like a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian British engineer of railways, bridges and steamships.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel's unusual first name is the obvious one to identify a famous engineer by.

clue.text: One camper wandering outside turned up 19 skeletons!

indicators.note: turned round means facing back, so the word is read backwards
being outside means surrounding, so the shuffled letters wrap round the short piece
wandering things stray from their path, so the letters move about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
being up at university is being at it

explanation.surface: A lost hiker stumbles across bones of the ill-fated character in 19.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 points to AT HAND, so the definition reads 'hand skeletons'.
explanation.definitionFit: The metacarpals are the five long bones forming the framework of the palm.

clue.text: Musical work, something groovy recalled with books

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A cool tune is remembered along with some books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' suggests sixties cool; it means having a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: Turandot is Puccini's last opera, a musical stage work.

clue.text: Element, mostly temporary one, we must think

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the sound made while pausing to think

explanation.surface: A stand-in chemist ponders which element might be the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinium is a radioactive metallic chemical element, number 89.

clue.text: Base display of arrogance greeting native American

parts.note: putting on airs is a show of arrogance
the traditional greeting attributed to Native Americans

explanation.surface: A haughty show of contempt towards a Native American's greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like low or contemptible, but it is an airbase.
explanation.definitionFit: An airshow is a flying display often held at an air force base.

clue.text: Coming soon, Jonathan Demme's Caged …

indicators.note: caged means held inside, so the letters lie within the words before it

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A trailer for a new Jonathan Demme film called Caged.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue, as if listing films.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at hand is near in time and imminent, about to arrive.

clue.text: Stretch one's mind with centre for reading

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the middle letter is kept

explanation.surface: Advice to broaden your mental horizons by reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell out by pressure from inside, a kind of stretching.

clue.text: … Heat, note, theatre putting out first showing a third time?

indicators.note: putting out the first means removing the opening letter

parts.note: re is a note of the scale
a rep is a repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre stages Heat for yet another run.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 19's film theme: Heat is a Michael Mann movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat is shown a second time, so a rerepeat would be a third showing.

clue.text: Bacteriologist favoured upping radiation

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A favourite scientist increases the radiation dose.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Petri was the German bacteriologist who gave his name to the culture dish.

clue.text: Bolts entrance to storehouse after derisory comment

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the one named later
an entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone padlocks the warehouse door after a sneering remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolts' suggests locks, but means gulping food down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, which is what bolting a meal means.

clue.text: Show of concern? Not to women on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: Worry about not sending the women on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown is a facial expression of worry or displeasure, displaying concern outwardly.

clue.text: Fixture, not ending all square

indicators.note: not ending means it stops short, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A match left unfinished with the scores level.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams that are even are level on points, which is what all square means.

clue.text: Hold-up as echo's smothered in order to be quiet

indicators.note: something smothered is covered over, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: hist is an old call for silence
Echo is E in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A robbery during which the echo is muffled to keep things silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, and hold-up is the everyday term for an armed theft.

clue.text: Something of a catch, daughter ended single

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter's single days are over: she is quite a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' sounds like an eligible partner, but means a fish landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a prized flatfish, so it forms part of a fisherman's haul.

clue.text: Such as spring camping I love that comes to bad end?

definitions.text: Such as spring camping I love that comes to bad end?

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoiled, so the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis

explanation.surface: A spring camping trip, lovingly planned, that goes horribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the road to hell is paved with good intentions, so a well-meant plan may end badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-meant plans proverbially lead to disaster, so such an innocent holiday that ends badly fits.
